ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7.version: gcc 2.96-ee-001003-1 (cc1), locally patched: realconv + lp7 + fsv3 + fsv4 + fsv5 + fsv6 + fsv7 + fsv8 + fsv9 + fsv10 + fsv12

rebuild: Download the base archive and check its SHA-256.
Extract lib/gcc-lib/ee/2.96-ee-001003-1/{cc1,cpp0} and bin/ee-gcc into <root>/ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv12-v1/bin/.
cpp0 and ee-gcc are used unmodified.

Apply the patches below to cc1, in file-offset order (nine single-byte patches and twenty multi-byte patches: fsv1, fsv3, fsv4, fsv5, fsv6, fsv7, fsv8, fsv9, fsv10 and fsv12); the result must hash to the cc1 SHA-256 above.

note: Each entry patches the bytes of the extracted cc1 at `file_offset` (one byte, except the fsv1, fsv3 and fsv4 entries, the 86-byte fsv5 gen_extendqidi2 entry, the three fsv6 entries, the four fsv7 entries, the two fsv8 entries, the fsv9 entry, the two fsv10 entries and the two fsv12 entries, which replace the given hex strings).
`old` must be the byte already there; `new` replaces it.
The six `realconv` patches turn the six MASK_MIPS5900 conversion gates
of the bundled e-type float code into unconditional jumps, so decimal
literals round the way the original compiler rounded them.
The two `lp7` patches raise the R5900 short-loop padding gate and loop
bound in mips_r5900_lengthen_loops from 4 to 6, which reproduces the
7-d padding ten original game objects carry.
The `fsv1` patch (user decision 2026-09-23, reports/cc1-fsv-clause1-losum.md)
rewrites clause 1 of the alias-analysis helper fixed_scalar_and_varying_struct_p
(cc1 0x080ee624) so that a LO_SUM address of the scalar mem1 counts as
non-varying: a store to a split (lui/%lo) global scalar no longer blocks a
later struct-field load with a varying address in sched1, as the original
CardMainProc (OV10 0x00A03AA0) shows. Clause 2 and rtx_varies_p are unchanged.
The three `fsv3` patches (user decision 2026-09-23, reports/cc1-fsv3-alias.md)
supersede fsv1 on top of it: clause 2 treats a LO_SUM mem2 address as non-varying
too (symmetric LO_SUM rule), and make_decl_rtl jumps to an 88-byte cave written
over debug_rtx_list (only called by the debug-only debug_rtx_find) that gives the
MEM of a non-function, non-small-data decl its type alias set by calling
set_mem_attributes before DECL_RTL is stored. The cave source is cave.s in the release.
The `fsv4` patch (user decision 2026-10-09, reports/cc1-fsv4-gcse-transp.md)
supersedes fsv3 on top of it: compute_transp (gcse.c, 0x080f30d6) passes
rtx_varies_p instead of rtx_addr_varies_p as the varies argument of
canon_true_dependence, so fixed_scalar_and_varying_struct_p can apply in gcse
load-PRE transparency: an in-struct store through a varying pointer no longer
kills a fixed scalar load. FSF gcse.c passes rtx_addr_varies_p there; the
original EE build is inferred to differ (MenuShopCore, main 0x0024EE80).
The two `fsv5` (qisi) patches (user decision 2026-10-10, reports/cc1-fsv5-qisi.md)
supersede fsv4 on top of it: recog_4 (0x08180772, je -> jmp) never recognizes
extendqidi2_insn, and gen_extendqidi2 (0x081a4514) expands a QI->DI sign
extension as extendqisi2 into a new SImode pseudo plus a separate extendsidi2
(86 bytes assembled from qisi.S in the release). A char widened to 64 bits is
then lb plus an in-place extendsidi2 that prints nothing but is counted by the
R5900 short-loop pass, as the original getStrIndex family (main tu145, tu148,
tu229, 0x002f6210) shows. FSF GCC fuses the two into extendqidi2_insn; the
original EE build is inferred to differ.
The three `fsv6` patches (release ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv6-v2, user decision 2026-10-27,
reports/cc1-fsv6-legit-addr.md, Rev 2) supersede fsv5 on top of it and remove two reads of
host heap garbage that made codegen depend on line-marker path lengths and
ASLR. mips_legitimate_address_p (0x081c184d, 20 bytes from legit.S) evaluates
its TARGET_64BIT `INTVAL (xplus1) > 0` clause only for a CONST_INT, so
SYMBOL_REF/CONST/LABEL_REF/HIGH sym(reg) addresses are accepted, as on the
original 32-bit host whose heap lay below 0x80000000 (ov11 VW_ViewModeInit,
VW_SamMode). gen_mem_addressof (0x08093e59, 15 bytes) jumps to a 28-byte cave
(0x081a4570, memalias.S, in the tail of gen_extendqidi2 unreachable since
fsv5) that clears MEM_ALIAS_SET (reg) before get_alias_set (decl), so an
address-taken VAR_DECL gets alias set 0 instead of the uninitialised high
word of the REG field it was converted from. Inferred from original bytes and
full six-unit identity, not from a recovered binary.
The four `fsv7` patches (release ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv7-v2, user decision 2026-10-27,
reports/cc1-fsv7-transp-argreg.md, section 8) supersede fsv6 on top of it: compute_transp
(gcse.c) calls transp_dep (0x081d5798) instead of canon_true_dependence at
0x080f30e6. transp_dep keeps the fsv4 decision (rtx_varies_p), except that an
in-struct store whose base register (bare REG or PLUS operand 0) has global
origin S - every SET of it loads (mem (symbol_ref S)) or copies a register
with origin S - against a load of (symbol_ref S) takes the FSF decision
(rtx_addr_varies_p): a struct store through a pointer loaded from global S
kills a later load of S (rule "SameG"; MenuShopCore and MenuShopModelMain
natural forms, main 0x0024EE80). The three caves (transp_org.S) overwrite
debugger-only functions: transp_dep over debug_print_page_list, reg_global_origin
over debug_rli (0x08082640) and chk over debug_candidates (0x0816a064). Empirical
model fitted on 27 decisive sites; no GCC 2.96 source mechanism is known.
The two `fsv8` patches (release ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv8-v1, user decision 2026-10-28,
reports/cc1-fsv8-nzinit.md) supersede fsv7 on top of it ("NZ-init"): in the fsv3 make_decl_rtl
cave the small-data jg at 0x080d92a2 (file 0x912a2, inside the fsv3 entry at 0x9127c,
so that entry applies first) jumps to a 54-byte cave at 0x080d92d4 (nzinit.S, over
the unreachable tail of debug_rtx_list and the debugger-only debug_rtx_range). A
small-data declaration whose DECL_INITIAL is non-null, not error_mark_node and not
integer_zerop then also gets its type alias set (set_mem_attributes), as every
non-small-data declaration does since fsv3; small-data declarations without an
initializer or with a zero one keep alias set 0. Empirical: one positive case
(sw in main tu097 xglJpegEncode/StartOfScan), neutral on 673 TUs.
The `fsv9` patch (release ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv9-v1, user decision 2026-10-29,
reports/cc1-fsv9-anyg.md) supersedes fsv8 on top of it ("AnyG"): in the fsv7-v2 compute_transp
cave transp_dep (over debug_print_page_list) the 5 bytes at 0x081d57e8 (file 0x18d7e8)
turn `cmp 0x4(%ebx),%eax; jne` (store base origin == the PRE load symbol) into
`test %eax,%eax; nop; je` (any global origin). An in-struct store through a pointer
loaded from any global then takes the FSF rtx_addr_varies_p decision for a load of a
global. Empirical: fsv7 named AnyG as equally consistent; main tu167 MenuFile is the
separating case. Neutral on 673 TUs.
The two `fsv10` patches (release ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv10-v1, user decision 2026-10-29,
reports/cc1-fsv10-swu.md) supersede fsv9 on top of it ("swu"): mems_conflict_for_gcse_p pushes
rtx_addr_varies_p at 0x080efe20 (file 0xa7e20); that push becomes a jump to a 38-byte cave
over the unreferenced debug_rtx_find at 0x080d9310 (file 0x91310). The cave pushes
rtx_varies_p when the store MEM (%edx) is SImode, has alias set 0 and MEM_IN_STRUCT_P,
rtx_addr_varies_p otherwise, and jumps back to 0x080efe25. Empirical, one positive case
(main tu167 MenuFile head store); neutral on 673 TUs.
The two `fsv12` patches (release ee-gcc2.96-realconv-lp7-fsv12-v1, user decision 2026-10-30,
reports/cc1-fsv12-r3split.md) supersede fsv10 on top of it ("R3"): the split_insns prologue at 0x08197798
(file 0x14f798) becomes a jump to a 286-byte cave over the unreferenced debug_candidate at
0x08169f0c (file 0x121f0c). After reload the cave splits (set (reg:SI R) SYM), SYM accepted by
mips_check_split, into (set R (high SYM)) + (set R (lo_sum R SYM)) when R is $16..$23 or $30
and a CALL_INSN precedes the insn in its basic block; otherwise it runs the replaced prologue
and jumps to 0x0819779e. Empirical surrogate, one positive case (main tu211 sefExecScheduler
prologue); neutral on 673 TUs and the live tree.
Why this is a patched binary and not a published one (public-compiler hunt,
2026-09-12, .work/attempts/tu-public-compiler-hunt/attempt-1/artifact.json):
all 15 public ee-gcc* entries of the pinned decompme catalog revision were
tested, and none produces both the rounded decimal literals and the 7-d
short-loop padding the original bytes carry. The flag hypothesis is dead
mechanically: the complete TARGET_SWITCHES/TARGET_OPTIONS tables were read
out of every candidate ELF and no entry names rounding, truncation, loops or
the R5900 short-loop erratum, and the padding pass is gated on the same
MASK_MIPS5900 bit with its thresholds as immediate bytes in code.
lp7's value is SCE's own: ps2-ee-toolchain ee/gcc/config/mips/mips.c:8717
(SCE 2.9-ee-991111, GPL-2.0-or-later) reads `for (; distance <= 6;
distance++) emit_insn_before (gen_nop (), insn);`, and the public
ee-gcc2.9-991111 cc1 carries `cmp $0x6` at 0x081ad7cc and 0x081ad7e4 - the
same two instruction slots these patches set to 6 in the 2.96 binary, whose
catalog build moved the pass after delay-slot filling, split it into a
JUMP_INSN and a SEQUENCE arm and lowered both to 4. So the patch restores a
constant SCE shipped rather than inventing one; the build that carries it on
the JUMP arm only is not public.
The asymmetry is evidenced from both sides: the ten 7-d objects require 6 on
the JUMP arm, and raising the SEQUENCE arm to 6 as well breaks 17 of the 101
accepted C TUs, so 4 there is required by the accepted corpus.
Caveat that keeps original_distribution_proven false: the unpatched public
cc1 currently compiles all 101 accepted TUs to identical assembly and passes
the whole-file gate, because the recovered corpus is still blind to both
patches (0 of its 71 decimal literals discriminate rounding, 0 TUs reach the
JUMP arm). The original bytes are not blind: 343 rounded-evidence constants
and the ten padded objects. A clean witness is xglRenderSyncMove (main
0x0022CC40, five nops, body 7, unfilled delay slot).

patch_reasons: md_convert_frag copies an expanded alternative over its own destination; memcpy corrupts the overlap on a modern libc, memmove does not.  Behaviour only, not an encoding change.
The vsqrt base opcode carries bits 21-22 = 01 in every original word, as GNU as 2.10-ee-001003-1 and ps2dev binutils encode it; the 2.9 table has 00 and assembles the wrong word silently.

append_insn moved every label pending before an instruction to after the hazard nops it inserts; the original objects keep such labels before the nop (14 mtc1 sites, e.g. CardMainProc 0x00A085E8), so the loop is removed (mips_emit_delays unchanged; user decision 2026-09-24, reports/as-la29-vsqrt-nolabel.md). The build embeds its absolute source paths; the pinned hash is this project's build from .work/tu-migration/as-nolabel-adopt/build/src/tc-mips.c.

macro() case M_LA_AB expanded `la $t,CONST($b)` with a signed 16-bit CONST as `li; addu`; GNU as 2.10-ee-001003-1 (the archive of the project cc1) assembles it as one `addiu $t,$b,CONST` (daddiu for dla), through the opcode-table alias `la t,o(b)` that upstream binutils 0c11417f (2002-08-09) turned into this macro() shortcut. Backported for breg != 0 and in-range constants only; out-of-range constants keep li + addu, which is the only form the original objects contain (user decision 2026-09-25, reports/as-la-imm16.md). The build embeds its absolute source paths; the pinned hash is this project's build from .work/tu-migration/as-la-imm-adopt/build/src/tc-mips.c.
